newsitem.title: USA: Missouri soybean harvest slightly behind normal.
newsitem.headline: Missouri soybean harvest slightly behind normal.

text.p: Missouri's soybean harvest continued to lag the five-year average pace as of Sunday, while corn harvesting was making normal progress, the state's Agriculture Statistics Service said.
Soybeans were 70 percent harvested, a week behind the five-year average of 82 percent. Progress ranged from 43 percent in the southeastern district to 92 percent in the southwestern district.
"The ripening process is virtually complete over the state except in the Bootheel where 89 percent is rated mature," the report said.

The corn harvest was 79 percent finished, the same as the five-year average. Harvesting was virtually complete across the southern third of the state and least advanced in the northeastern district where it stood at just 62 percent done.
Sorghum was eighty percent harvested, marginally down on the five-year average of 81 percent.
Seventy-eight percent of winter wheat had been seeded, about a day behind the normal 79 percent.
Wheat was rated nine percent excellent, 56 percent good, 33 percent fair and two percent poor.
